input.question: How do TV shows maintain their "style" when they seem to switch directors with every episode?
input.ground_truth: I'll use Supernatural as an example. The scripts for the entire season are already written, as that is the main step in pre-production. Depending on how the show is setup, there may be one director contracted to direct X amount of episodes, and the rest is really up to the Executive Producer/Showrunner. [This](_URL_0_) page breaks down every Supernatural episode and who directed it, and almost every single episode this season has been directed by a different person. So each director simply follows the script and is able to give their own stylistic variation, even if you don't see it. If you're adept in the TV world, you notice subtle changes.

Question: How do TV shows maintain their "style" when they seem to switch directors with every episode?

Okay, let’s imagine a TV show is like a big family that always wears the same color T-shirts, even though different people help them get ready every day.

Each episode of a TV show is like a different day. Even though a different “helper” (director) is in charge each day, they all follow the same rules the family made. These rules are like, “We always wear blue shirts,” or “We always eat breakfast together.” 

For a TV show, the “rules” are things like how the show looks, sounds, and feels. The directors and the people who make the show talk about these rules and follow them, so every episode looks and feels the same, even if a different person is in charge that day. That’s how the show keeps its style!
